Obtain an Aramco/OGJ master-gas-system network schematic that actually names line 'UA-1' or a km-post-199->Uthmaniyah segment before confirming; simultaneously run a de-dup/segmentation review of the whole P1897-P1925 km-post cluster (esp. against P1907, P1905) to decide whether these are distinct pipes or double-counted segments of one Ghawar->Uthmaniyah Khuff-gas system.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE (primary concern). The name 'UA-1-km199-Uthmaniya' is a GIS/network-segment label, not a name any independent source uses: 'UA-1' reads as a line/route code and 'km199' as a kilometer post. A targeted search of the exact string returns ONLY the gem.wiki page itself (no independent hit). The gem.wiki row's only cited sources (from wiki_citations.json) are OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletin 2012 (p.75) and ASB 2017 (p.92) -- these are NATIONAL AGGREGATE statistics tables (reserves, output, refinery/pipeline-network totals) that do NOT name individual pipelines, so they do not corroborate the existence of this specific line. No independent EN/trade source (Aramco, MEED, Argaam, OGJ) names it. GulfPub's PE World Map Saudi gas roster (20 features -- GulfPub's best-covered country) contains NO Uthmaniya line at all; it captures the major trunks (MGS/MGS2/MGS3, East-West, Qatif-Berri, Abqaiq-Qatif) but none of these km-post gathering segments, consistent with them being sub-transmission network detail rather than independently documented pipelines. This row is one of ~29 similarly km-post/junction-named rows (P1897 A47-Yanbu, P1898/P1899 UBTG-1-Berri, P1900 UBTG-km56-AY-1 KP916, P1901 UBTG-1km-Juanymah, P1903 AY-1 KP943-Riyadh, etc.) bulk-imported 2022-07-19, all with the same weak OPEC-ASB sourcing pattern. The PHYSICAL pipe almost certainly exists -- Uthmaniyah is a real, long-operating Aramco Khuff-gas processing plant in the central Ghawar / Eastern Province area, fed by real gathering trunks -- so status='operating' is plausible; but as an INDEPENDENTLY-DOCUMENTED NAMED PIPELINE this does not verify, and sourcing is effectively GEM-derived only. SECONDARY concern -- DUPLICATE/SEGMENTATION: this row shares an identical spec fingerprint (len ~108/124 km, diameter '24, 32' in, terminus Uthmaniya) with P1907 (Haradh-3-Uthmaniya, 124 km, 24/32 in) and sits in the same Haradh/Hawiyah->Uthmaniyah Khuff-gas corridor as P1905 (Haradh-Uthmaniya, 140 km, 48 in) and P1915 (Hawiyah-Uthmaniya, 47 km); the km-post naming strongly suggests these are segments of one network at risk of double-counting. ATTRIBUTION: Owner=Saudi Aramco 100% is correct in kind (all Master Gas System infrastructure is Aramco-owned/operated) but is not independently sourced to this line. SPEC: none of length=108, diameter='24, 32', or endpoints could be corroborated against any independent source -- the numbers trace only to GEM. Confirmed independently: Uthmaniyah is a genuine Aramco gas-processing plant in the Eastern Province Ghawar area (Wikipedia Ghawar Field, verified).

routes.corridor_desc: Only the terminus is defensibly locatable. The line ends at Aramco's Uthmaniyah gas-processing plant in the central Ghawar / Al-Ahsa area of the Eastern Province (~25.19N, 49.31E, per OpenStreetMap/mapcarta node W764611169). The stated ~108 km length and the 'UA-1 / km-post 199' start imply a segment of Aramco's Master Gas System gathering trunk running through the Ghawar corridor (Ain Dar/Shedgum -> Uthmaniyah -> Hawiyah -> Haradh production areas) toward the Uthmaniyah plant, but the start endpoint is an unnamed kilometer post with no sourceable coordinate. Bound loosely: a ~108 km corridor within the Eastern Province Ghawar area terminating at Uthmaniyah; the upstream end and exact path are NOT sourced. No coordinates fabricated for the start/waypoints.
routes.researcher_notes: End endpoint (Uthmaniyah gas plant) coordinate taken from OpenStreetMap node W764611169 (25.18769N, 49.30634E), verified via mapcarta and database.earth; Uthmaniyah as a real Aramco gas-processing area independently confirmed by Wikipedia Ghawar Field. Start endpoint is a km-post label ('UA-1', km199) with no independent name or coordinate -- left null rather than fabricated. Corridor described in prose only; no route geometry proposed for a routes-repo PR beyond the sourced terminus.
